**Item #:** SCP-TEST-003

**Object Class:** Keter

**Special Containment Procedures:** Due to the nature of SCP-TEST-003, containment focuses on information suppression and rapid response protocols.

**Description:** SCP-TEST-003 is an anomalous phenomenon affecting written communication. When specific patterns are written, they trigger temporary memory loss in readers.

@@ @@
----
@@ @@

**Addendum TEST-003-A:** Interview Log

> **Interviewed:** Dr. Sarah Chen
>
> **Interviewer:** Agent Marcus Webb
>
> **Date:** ██/██/2015
>
> ----
>
> **<BEGIN LOG>**
>
> **Agent Webb:** Please describe what happened on the day of the incident.
>
> **Dr. Chen:** I was reviewing the documents in Lab 7. Around 14:00, I noticed something odd about the formatting.
>
> **Agent Webb:** Can you be more specific?
>
> **Dr. Chen:** The words seemed to... shift. Like they were rearranging themselves on the page.
>
> **Agent Webb:** And then?
>
> **Dr. Chen:** I don't remember. The next thing I knew, it was three hours later and I was in the medical bay.
>
> **(pause)**
>
> **Agent Webb:** Thank you, Dr. Chen. That will be all for now.
>
> **<END LOG>**

@@ @@
----
@@ @@

**Addendum TEST-003-B:** Research Notes

> +++ Preliminary Findings
>
> Initial analysis suggests SCP-TEST-003 operates through a combination of visual and cognitive mechanisms:
>
> # Pattern recognition triggers an anomalous response in the brain
> # The response causes temporary disruption of short-term memory formation
> # Recovery typically occurs within 1-6 hours
>
> Further research is required to understand the full scope of SCP-TEST-003's effects.
